title: Chapter 37 — Sunset
paragraphs: The cabin, by the stern windows. Ahab sitting alone, gazing out.
I leave a white and troubled wake. Pale waters, paler cheeks, wherever I sail. The jealous waves swell sideways to swallow my track. Let them — but first I pass.

Out there, at the ever-brimming goblet's rim, the warm waves blush like wine. The golden brow plumbs the blue. The diver sun — slowly dived from noon — goes down. My soul mounts up! She tires of her endless hill. Is, then, the crown too heavy that I wear? This Iron Crown of Lombardy. Yet it is bright with many a gem. I, the wearer, cannot see its distant flashing — but I darkly feel that I wear something that dazzlingly confounds. It is iron — that I know — not gold. It is cracked, too — I feel it. The jagged edge chafes me so, my brain seems to beat against the solid metal. Yes, a steel skull, mine — the kind that needs no helmet in the most brain-battering fight!

Dry heat upon my brow? Oh! There was a time when the sunrise nobly stirred me and the sunset soothed. No more. This lovely light — it doesn't light me. All beauty is agony to me, since I can never enjoy it. Gifted with the high perception, I lack the low, enjoying power. Damned — most subtly and most cruelly! Damned in the midst of Paradise! Good night — good night! (Waving his hand, he moves from the window.)

It was not so hard a task. I expected to find at least one man stubborn, but my one geared circle fits into all their various wheels, and they revolve. Or, if you prefer, like so many anthills of gunpowder, they all stand before me — and I am their match. Oh, how hard! That to set others ablaze, the match itself must burn away! What I have dared, I have willed. And what I have willed, I will do! They think me mad — Starbuck does. But I am demonic. I am madness maddened! That wild madness that is calm only to comprehend itself! The prophecy said I would be dismembered — and yes! I lost this leg. I now prophesy that I will dismember my dismemberer. So let the prophet and the fulfiller be one. That's more than you great gods ever were. I laugh at you and hoot at you, you cricket-players, you boxers, you deaf Burkes and blinded Bendigoes! I will not say as schoolboys say to bullies: pick on someone your own size, don't pummel me! No — you've knocked me down, and I am up again. But you have run and hidden. Come out from behind your cotton bags! I have no long gun to reach you. Come, Ahab sends his compliments — come and see if you can swerve me. Swerve me? You cannot swerve me — or else you swerve yourselves! There, man has you. Swerve me? The path to my fixed purpose is laid with iron rails, and my soul is grooved to run on them. Over unsounded gorges, through the rifled hearts of mountains, under the beds of torrents, I rush unerringly! Nothing is an obstacle, nothing is an angle on the iron way!
